summary: Iodine is needed to make thyroid hormones, which support metabolism and development.

deficiency.overview: Low iodine can impair thyroid-hormone production. Pregnancy and diets excluding seafood, dairy and eggs need appropriate professional assessment.
deficiency.medicalBoundary: Symptoms are nonspecific and cannot diagnose a nutrient deficiency. Diagnosis may require clinical evaluation and appropriate laboratory testing.

excess.overview: High iodine intake can also harm thyroid function. Deficiency and excess can share symptoms, so symptoms cannot guide self-dosing.
excess.medicalBoundary: No upper limit is an intake goal. Seek professional or medical advice before changing supplement or medication use.

interactions.counterparty: Medicines discussed in the linked NIH ODS fact sheet
interactions.description: Iodine supplements can interact with antithyroid medicines. Potassium iodide can raise potassium with ACE inhibitors or potassium-sparing diuretics.
interactions.limitations: Informational summary, not a complete interaction list or an instruction to change medicines.
